verdict: READY TO MERGE - 14 of 14 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: test_session_bookmark_notes_contract.py pins every value notes.ts copies (path, version, both limits, default state_dir) against the script and against both defaults.json and a real unconfigured project, so a one-sided edit fails.
The state_dir test in bookmark.test.ts places a decoy notes file under the default dir, so it proves the configured dir wins rather than merely being reachable.
test_add_note_script.py is fully behavioral: it runs the real script against make_project git repos and inspects the file on disk, with no stubs of the code under test.
notes.test.ts covers parseNotes' edge cases (wrong version, non-array notes, mixed entry types, per-note truncation, newest-kept overflow) as pure-function tests.
'a precompute reads no notes' asserts on recorded fs reads, guarding the INSTALLING filter against an extra file read on every precompute.

notes.ts is pure, copies the shared names and limits, and points to a contract test that pins them against add_note.py, which is how an installed mod can stay in sync with the harness plugin it cannot import.
captureNotes keeps the hook's never-throws contract: each fs read has its own catch, the loop sits in a try, and a notes failure only leaves the section out of the bookmark.
The notes file is anchored at the git top level on both sides (project_root in Python, rev-parse --show-toplevel in the mod), so a session in a linked worktree reads the same file the skill wrote.
write_notes writes a sibling temp file and then calls os.replace, so a compaction never reads a half-written notes file.

Limits (20 notes, 300 characters), file name, schema version and default state_dir agree across add_note.py, notes.ts, the agent, the skill and both READMEs, and a contract test pins them on both sides.
The agent states the note is data, not an instruction, and forbids quotes, backticks and $ in the single-quoted shell argument, closing the obvious injection route.
session-bookmark README documents the shared-per-project and per-worktree behavior as a known limitation instead of leaving it to be discovered.
Writer (project_root: cwd git top level first) and reader (rootCandidates: cwd first, git --show-toplevel) resolve the same file in the repository case, including linked worktrees.

Cross-plugin contract is pinned: test_session_bookmark_notes_contract.py ties NOTES_PATH, version, limits and the default state_dir in notes.ts to add_note.py and defaults.json, and round-trips a stored note through the script.

Notes resolution matches on both sides for worktrees: add_note.py uses project_root (git top level of cwd) and the mod reads under the same `--show-toplevel`, with a bookmark test proving a linked worktree reads its own file.
The mod's capture stays fail-open: captureNotes swallows every read/parse failure, and tests cover absent, malformed and other-version files plus the no-git fallback to root candidates.
add_note.py tests are behavioral against real files built with make_project (cap, full file, malformed file, atomic write leaving no temp file), with no mocking of the code under test.
Docs move together: root README, session-bookmark README, plugin descriptions, Bookmark type and both plugin versions are updated in the same change.

important.name: bookmark-noter assumes its prompt is the bare arguments, but a context: fork skill sends the whole SKILL.md body
important.summary:
bookmark-noter.md:5-6 says the prompt is 'the developer's arguments after /add-bookmark' and lines 37-44 dispatch on 'the first word' of the prompt, with a 'nothing' row for an empty prompt. add-bookmark/SKILL.md:6-7 sets context: fork with agent: harness:bookmark-noter, so the forked agent's prompt is the rendered skill body (heading, two prose paragraphs, 'Arguments: `...`', and its own arguments table). Read literally, the first word is '#', every invocation falls into 'anything else', and the 'nothing' row can never fire because an empty $ARGUMENTS still yields a non-empty prompt ('Arguments: ``'). The agent only works if the model infers where the arguments sit; the sibling messenger agent (agents/messenger.md:32-41) is written for exactly this skill-body prompt shape.

Also (docs): bookmark-noter.md:44 puts `usage: /add-bookmark <note> | --list | --clear` in a table cell; GFM splits cells on pipes even inside code spans, so the row renders with extra columns and a truncated usage string. The root README escapes the same case as `1\|2\|3` (README.md:19). The usage string also names /add-bookmark while the installed command is /harness:add-bookmark (README.md:99, session-bookmark README.md:23).

Also (overall): The `nothing` row's cell holds `usage: /add-bookmark <note> | --list | --clear` inside a code span; GFM splits cells on those pipes even in code spans, so the row renders as five cells and the reply text is mangled. The usage also names `/add-bookmark` while README and SKILL document the invocation as `/harness:add-bookmark`.
fix: Reword bookmark-noter.md lines 5-6 and 37 to say the prompt is the add-bookmark skill body and the action is chosen by the first word of the text inside 'Arguments: `...`' (empty backticks = the 'nothing' row).
Alternatively shrink SKILL.md's body to just the arguments line so the prompt matches what the agent describes, keeping the explanatory prose in the description or a comment the fork does not send.
Escape the pipes: `usage: /harness:add-bookmark <note> \| --list \| --clear`.
Or move the usage reply out of the table into a sentence below it.
Escape the pipes (`\|`) or move the usage line below the table, and write it as `usage: /harness:add-bookmark <note> | --list | --clear`.

important.name: Worktree notes test cannot tell the git top level from the first root candidate
important.summary: The test 'notes are read from the git top level, so a worktree reads its own' sets cwd to the worktree root itself, and the fake gitAnswer (line 59) answers rev-parse --show-toplevel with the very folder it was asked about. So top == first candidate (rootCandidates puts cwd first), and no notes file exists at ROOT. A mutation of captureNotes in bookmark.ts:172-177 that ignores `top` and always walks rootCandidates still passes. The test therefore cannot fail for the behavior in its title. It also hard-codes '.claude/state/harness' instead of DEFAULT_STATE_DIR.
fix: Let World map a folder to its top level (e.g. `tops?: Record<string, string>`), have gitAnswer return that for rev-parse --show-toplevel, and accept the subfolder as a repo. Then set cwd to '/wt/feature/sub', keep CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR at ROOT, put one notes file under '/wt/feature' and another under ROOT, and expect only the worktree note. Build the path from DEFAULT_STATE_DIR.

important.name: formatBookmark crashes on a bookmark stored before this change
important.summary: formatBookmark reads `b.notes.length` unguarded (bookmark.ts:113). The bookmark lives in `$.state`, which the module header says outlives compaction and module reloads, and the atom has no version. A session that compacted under the previous mod version and then reloads the updated plugin holds a Bookmark with no `notes` key. `/session-bookmark` then calls formatBookmark on it (bookmark.ts:241) and throws TypeError instead of printing the bookmark. The `.catch` at line 242 hangs off the `on(...)` registration, not the handler, so nothing in the handler catches the throw.
fix: Guard the read: `const notes = b.notes ?? []` in formatBookmark and use `notes` for both the length check and noteLines.
Normalise in the command handler before formatting: `formatBookmark({ ...b, notes: b.notes ?? [] })`, and add a test that formats a bookmark object without `notes`.

important.name: Subcommand check in the agent guard test cannot fail
important.summary:
test_agent_names_the_script_and_each_subcommand searches the agent body for  add ,  list  and  clear . The same test already requires 'skills/add-bookmark/commands/add_note.py' (line 69), and `-` is a word boundary, so 'add-bookmark' always satisfies  add . 'list' and 'clear' appear in the description prose ('store, list or clear'). Dropping every subcommand row from the agent's Arguments table (bookmark-noter.md:41-43) leaves the loop green.

Also (overall): test_agent_names_the_script_and_each_subcommand searches the agent body for  add ,  list  and  clear . Those words match inside `/add-bookmark`, `--list` and `--clear` (a hyphen is a word boundary), which the agent prose names regardless of whether it ever runs `NOTE add`, `NOTE list` or `NOTE clear`. Dropping or renaming the script subcommands in bookmark-noter.md (for example `NOTE append`) leaves the test green, so the guard does not pin the agent-to-script contract its docstring claims.

Also (tests): The module docstring says the test pins 'the limits they share' across the skill, the agent and the script. But test_agent_states_the_script_limits checks only the agent, while SKILL.md:17 also states 'at most 20 notes, at most 300 characters' and can drift unnoticed. `str(script.MAX_NOTES) in body` is a bare '20' substring, so any year, PR number or count satisfies it.
fix: Assert the command forms the agent actually issues: `for sub in ('add', 'list', 'clear'): assert f'NOTE {sub}' in body`.
Assert the exact command forms the agent runs: `NOTE add`, `NOTE list`, `NOTE clear` (e.g. `for sub in ("add", "list", "clear"): assert f"NOTE {sub}" in body`).
Or parse the add_note.py subparser names (script.parse_args) and assert each appears as `NOTE <name>` in the agent body.

Check both texts with phrase regexes: `re.search(rf'at most {script.MAX_NOTES} notes', text)` and `re.search(rf'at most {script.MAX_NOTE_CHARS} characters', text)` for SKILL.md and bookmark-noter.md (both currently carry those exact phrases).

important.name: No test for a notes file with one bad entry or another version; add silently discards stored notes
important.summary: test_a_malformed_file_is_replaced_not_fatal only covers invalid JSON. add_note.read_notes (add_note.py:41-50) returns [] when any single entry lacks a string text, and it never checks `version`. As a result, `list` says 'no notes' while the mod's parseNotes (notes.ts:59-64) still prints the good entries. `add` then overwrites the file, dropping every valid note, and it rewrites a version-2 file as version 1. The two readers of one file disagree, and no test pins either case.
fix: Add tests to test_add_note_script.py: (a) a file whose notes mix one valid entry with `5`/`null` entries, where `list` shows the valid one and `add` keeps it; (b) a version-2 file, where `add` exits 1 (or otherwise leaves the file untouched). Align read_notes with parseNotes so both pass: filter bad entries instead of rejecting the list, and treat a foreign version as not writable.

minor.name: state_dir key row omits the new session-notes consumer
minor.summary:
README.md:188 lists state_dir as holding 'Phase 5 sentinels, pr-team runtime'. This PR stores session notes there (add_note.py:38) and the session-bookmark mod now reads state_dir from harness.json (notes.ts:34-38), so a project that relocates state_dir changes where notes live in both plugins. Separately, README.md:23 phrases the cap as 'at most 20 of 300 characters', which reads as a fraction rather than 20 notes of up to 300 characters each.

Also (overall): The session-bookmark mod now reads `state_dir` from `.claude/harness.json` and mirrors its default (DEFAULT_STATE_DIR in hooks/notes.ts). CLAUDE.md's config-key rule says a mod that reads a key mirrors its default in `hooks/config.ts`, checked by `tests/mods/test_<mod>_config_mirror.py`; this PR places the mirror in notes.ts and checks it in test_session_bookmark_notes_contract.py instead, and the README key table's `state_dir` row (README.md:188) still lists only `Phase 5 sentinels, pr-team runtime` as consumers.
fix: README.md:188 used-by column: 'Phase 5 sentinels, pr-team runtime, session-bookmark notes (gitignore it)'; README.md:23: '(at most 20 notes, 300 characters each)'.

Add `session-bookmark notes (`session-bookmark/notes.json`)` to the `state_dir` row's consumers in README.md:188, and either note in CLAUDE.md that the notes contract test is session-bookmark's mirror check or move DEFAULT_STATE_DIR into a `hooks/config.ts` with a `test_session_bookmark_config_mirror.py`.

minor.name: Reply contract lists output shapes the script does not print
minor.summary: bookmark-noter.md:59 names the replies as 'note N/20: <line>', the numbered list, or 'cleared N notes'. add_note.py:83 prints 'no notes' for an empty list and add_note.py:89 prints 'cleared 1 note' (singular) for one note. A haiku agent told to relay one of three shapes 'and nothing else' may treat the other outputs as unexpected.
fix: Change bookmark-noter.md:59 to: The script's output (`note N/20: <line>`, the numbered list or `no notes`, or `cleared N note(s)`), verbatim, and nothing else.

minor.name: add silently overwrites a notes file it cannot parse
minor.summary:
read_notes returns [] for a present but malformed file, or one holding a single bad entry, and treats it the same as a missing file (add_note.py:41-50). add then writes `[new note]` over it (add_note.py:73-77), so one hand edit that breaks the JSON or one non-text entry drops every stored note without a warning. read_notes also ignores `version`, while the mod's parseNotes rejects any version other than 1 (notes.ts:61). A file of another version is listed and appended to here but rewritten as version 1, and the bookmark prints none of it.

Also (overall): add_note.py read_notes returns [] for the whole file when any one entry lacks a string `text`, and never checks `version`. notes.ts parseNotes drops only the bad entries and rejects a file whose version is not 1. Consequences: `--list` prints `no notes` while the bookmark prints the valid ones; `add` on such a file silently rewrites it with only the new note, discarding every valid note; and a non-v1 file is listed and appended to by the script but ignored by the mod (README and SKILL both promise `--list` shows what the bookmark carries).
fix: Separate absent from malformed: return [] only on FileNotFoundError. Raise NoteError for undecodable JSON, a missing or non-list `notes`, a bad entry or `version != NOTES_VERSION`, so `add` refuses and `clear` stays the explicit reset.
Keep the tolerant read for `list`, but make `add` refuse when the file exists and read_notes found nothing usable in it.
Make read_notes mirror parseNotes: require version == NOTES_VERSION and keep the entries whose `text` is a non-blank string instead of discarding the list.
Or refuse (NoteError) to add to a file it cannot fully parse instead of overwriting it, and report that in `list`.

minor.name: session-bookmark README intro and first bullet still describe the pre-notes inputs
minor.summary:
session-bookmark README.md:3 says the bookmark is 'kept in session state instead of a file' and line 6 says 'it reads git state and the conversation'; the mod now also reads .claude/harness.json and <state_dir>/session-bookmark/notes.json. README.md:11-13 lists the recorded fields without notes, though the State table at line 46 was updated to include them. README.md:25-26 says the git calls are the compaction's only wait, while bookmark.ts capture() now also awaits the two file reads.

Also (overall): The README still says the mod reads only `git state and the conversation` (lines 6-7) and the first bullet lists what is recorded without the notes (lines 11-13). After this PR the mod also reads `.claude/harness.json` and `<state_dir>/session-bookmark/notes.json`, a file written by the harness plugin, so `depends on no other mod` needs the caveat that the notes feature needs harness's add-bookmark skill.
fix: Line 6: 'it reads git state, the conversation and the project's session-notes file'; line 13: add 'the stored session notes' before 'and the /compact instructions'; line 26: 'the git calls and the notes read are the compaction's only wait'.

Lines 6-7: `it reads git state, the conversation and the harness notes file (`.claude/harness.json` for `state_dir`); notes need the harness plugin's add-bookmark skill, the rest depends on no other plugin.` Lines 11-13: add `the session notes` before `and the /compact instructions`.

minor.name: Notes lookup order described backwards for the no-repository case
minor.summary: session-bookmark README.md:20-21 says the notes file is read under '(`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` and the cwd when neither is a repository)'. bookmark.ts captureNotes walks rootCandidates, which is cwd first, then CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, taking the first that holds a notes file; the writer (project.py:18-29 via add_note.py:33-38) picks CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR over cwd when neither is a repository. The parenthetical names the order the writer uses, not the reader's, and hides that the two can disagree when cwd also holds a stale notes file.
fix: Reword README.md:20-21 to: under the git top level of the session cwd, else of CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; when neither is a repository, the first of the cwd and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR that holds a notes file.

minor.name: Missing space after `=` in NOTES_FILE
minor.summary: `const NOTES_FILE =`${ROOT}/...`` lacks the space every other declaration in the file has.
fix: Write `const NOTES_FILE = `${ROOT}/${DEFAULT_STATE_DIR}/${NOTES_PATH}``.

minor.name: Python side of the shared git-top-level anchor is untested
minor.summary: The mod reads notes at the git top level, and the script resolves `--repo` through project_root (git top level). Every script test passes the project root itself, so a regression that stores under a subdirectory passed as --repo would go unnoticed by both test files, and the mod would read an empty bookmark.
fix: Add a test that creates `project/sub`, runs `add` with `--repo project/sub`, and asserts the file lands at `project/.claude/state/harness/session-bookmark/notes.json`.

minor.name: Script tests miss the cap boundary, the write side of a refusal, and the version constant
minor.summary: test_add_creates_the_file... asserts `data['version'] == 1` instead of script.NOTES_VERSION. test_text_past_the_cap_is_refused never checks that no file was written. No test shows that a note of exactly MAX_NOTE_CHARS is accepted, so an off-by-one (`>=`) in checked_text would pass.
fix: Use script.NOTES_VERSION on line 43; add `assert not (project / _NOTES_REL).exists()` after the refusal on line 72; add a test that `'x' * script.MAX_NOTE_CHARS` returns 0 and is stored.

minor.name: Root README lacks add-bookmark usage documentation
minor.summary: The root README shows one add-bookmark invocation in the workflow example block but never describes the add, --list and --clear forms, the note cap, where notes are stored, or what the compaction bookmark prints, so the new feature has no usage examples.
fix: Add a short add-bookmark subsection to README.md with usage examples for add, --list and --clear, the note and character limits, the notes file location under state_dir, and a pointer to plugins/session-bookmark/README.md for the bookmark output.
